title: Finite-field curves admit a projective closure
statement:
Let $k_0$ be a field and let $U_0$ be an integral separated scheme of
finite type over $k_0$ of dimension at most one. There are an integer $N$,
a locally closed immersion $a:U_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_{k_0}$,
and an integral projective scheme $X_0$ such that $a$ identifies
$U_0$ with a dense open subscheme of $X_0$, its scheme-theoretic
closure in $\mathbf P^N_{k_0}$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-dim-one-quasi-projective] to $U_0/k_0$: separatedness, finite type and $\dim U_0\leq1$ are precisely its hypotheses (the topological Krull dimension of the item [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] equals the supremum of the dimensions of the local rings by [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings], so the bound holds in either reading of that node's dimension). Obtain $N\geq0$, a scheme $V$, a closed immersion $i:U_0\hookrightarrow V$ and an open immersion $e:V\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Proj}(k_0[x_0,\ldots,x_N])$ over $k_0$. That node's projective space is $\operatorname{Proj}(k_0[x_0,\ldots,x_N])$ [def-pc-proj], while the item, [def-kun-projective] and step 2 use $P:=\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,N\};\operatorname{Spec}k_0)=\operatorname{Spec}k_0\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Proj}(\mathbf Z[T_0,\ldots,T_N])$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Apply [lem-nagata-affine-proj-scalar-extension] with $R=\mathbf Z$, $S=k_0$, $A=\mathbf Z[T_0,\ldots,T_N]$, $B=k_0[x_0,\ldots,x_N]$ and the graded $k_0$-algebra isomorphism $\beta:k_0\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A\to B$, $c\otimes T_m\mapsto cx_m$: the square formed by $r_\psi$, $p_B$, $p_A$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbf Z\to k_0)$ is cartesian, so $(p_B,r_\psi)$ is an isomorphism $\varphi:\operatorname{Proj}(B)\xrightarrow{\sim}P$ whose composite with the first projection $\pi:P\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ is $p_B$. Then $\varphi e$ is again an open immersion, and $a:=\varphi e i:U_0\hookrightarrow P$ is a locally closed immersion over $k_0$. No smoothness, perfectness or algebraic closedness is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0A25, lemma-dim-1-quasi-projective; first paragraph of Tag 0BXV, lemma-dim-1-projective-completion; identification of P^N_k with the base change of P^N_Z: constructions.tex Tag 01NF, definition-projective-space, and Tag 01N2, lemma-base-change-map-proj

proof.text: By [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], the projection $\pi:P\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ is proper, hence separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Since $\pi a$ is the given finite-type structure map, [lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target](b) shows that $a$ is finite type and in particular quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 01NH, lemma-projective-space-separated; schemes.tex Tag 03GI, lemma-quasi-compact-permanence; morphisms.tex Tag 01T8, lemma-permanence-finite-type

proof.text: Set $X_0=\operatorname{SIm}(a)$ with its closed immersion $\iota:X_0\hookrightarrow P$ [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]. The canonical factor $j:U_0\to X_0$ satisfies $\iota j=a$ [def-nagata-scheme-image-factor]. Since $a$ is a quasi-compact immersion, [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image] makes $j$ an open immersion with dense image. Thus this $X_0$ is the required scheme-theoretic closure.

Integrality of $U_0$ includes reducedness [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Since $a$ is quasi-compact (step 2), [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc] says that the map $\mathcal O_{X_0}\to j_*\mathcal O_{U_0}$ given by the factor map $j=a^{\mathrm{im}}$ is injective on sections: for every open $W\subseteq X_0$ the ring map $\mathcal O_{X_0}(W)\to\mathcal O_{U_0}(j^{-1}W)$ is injective. If $s\in\mathcal O_{X_0}(W)$ is nilpotent, its image is a nilpotent element of the reduced ring $\mathcal O_{U_0}(j^{-1}W)$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme], hence zero, so $s=0$. Thus every ring of sections of $X_0$ is reduced, and $X_0$ is reduced by the equivalent form in [def-pc-reduced-scheme].

source.place: Tag 01R8, lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image (1)-(2): for quasi-compact f the image is cut out by the kernel of O_Y -> f_*O_X; reducedness as in Tag 056B, lemma-scheme-theoretic-image-reduced

proof.text: The nonempty $U_0$ gives a point of $X_0$. If $X_0=F\cup G$ with $F,G$ closed, then $U_0=j^{-1}F\cup j^{-1}G$. Irreducibility of $U_0$ forces one inverse image to be all of $U_0$. The corresponding closed set contains the dense image of $j$, hence is $X_0$. Thus $X_0$ is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components]; with reducedness from step 4, [def-pc-integral-scheme] proves it integral.

source.place: Final sentence: integrality and density; explicit closed-cover argument

proof.text: Give $X_0$ the structure morphism $\pi\iota$. Its displayed closed embedding into $\mathbf P^N_{k_0}$ makes it projective by [def-kun-projective]. Moreover $(\pi\iota)j=\pi a$ is the original structure map, so all maps are over $k_0$. The chosen $N,a,X_0,\iota,j$ therefore satisfy every requested clause.

lean.statement:
theorem IsCurve.exists_projectiveClosure (p : U ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [IsCurve p] [IsIntegral U] :
    ∃ (n : Type u) (_ : Finite n) (X : Scheme.{u}) (ι : X ⟶ ℙ(n; Spec (.of K))) (j : U ⟶ X),
      IsClosedImmersion ι ∧ IsOpenImmersion j ∧ IsIntegral X ∧ DenseRange j.base ∧
      j ≫ ι ≫ (ℙ(n; Spec (.of K)) ↘ Spec (.of K)) = p
